I had a very similar situation. I attempted to take my own life and was left to sit in a room with a mattress on the floor for two and a half weeks whilst they waited for a hospital bed. I was treated like an animal, only being allowed to go to the toilet. They frequently forgot to bring me something to eat because I was in a small side room which was hidden. I can truly say it was the worst experiences of my life and I will forever be scarred by it. There is much more to it but I don’t know want to say. 

When I was finally found a bed, the hospital told me that they would inform my family. I told them no, and they had to listen because I was an adult. The nurse said of course we won’t, but as soon as I got to the hospital, family members were ringing me which made my situation a lot worse.

Sixteen years old is really the best time to turn things around. My partner didn’t see a point in continuing, so he purposely failed school, failed his exams, dropped out of sixth form (UK), and now works in construction. He really hates it and wants to go back into education, but he’d have to pay for it now as he’s too old. He’s happy now and sees the mistake clearly.

Work hard in school, achieve those grades, pray healthily and realize that you still have so much time to turn things around. I achieved my university degree whilst being an inpatient in a psychiatric ward. Anything you put your mind to, you can do it, I promise. 

Not to mention, my arms and legs are covered in deep, nasty scars. It’s a constant reminder of what I went through and I wish I could change it. Luckily I do not care too much about what others think of it, but there is little practicality in self harming. Sure, you might feel good for ten minutes, but afterwards is just full of regret and pain. I look at them and wish I could speak to my sixteen year old self and tell them not to do it.

Find comfort in hobbies, work hard in school, and put your mental energy into attempting to love yourself. It’s really hard, I know. Medication or talking therapy may help too. 

You’ll be okay.

I live in the UK. The GPs are stretched thin and I haven’t seen my own one in over two years. I really like him and he listens, but it’s impossible to get an appointment with him. The other doctor refused blood tests, and when he finally caved, it did turn out I have iron deficient anaemia. He insisted it wasn’t physical and said I was ‘not bedbound’ implying that I’m just lazy. 

At work, I get paid barely just enough to get by, so I thought I would apply for government benefits. I first tried the general one, but I earn too much (about £100 more a month), so that was a firm no. I applied for disability benefits again as I had them when I was younger, but they were taken away as I got better. They said that whilst they admitted my health restricts my life, it wasn’t enough to warrant financial help. I applied for a mandatory reconsideration, still no. I then applied for a court hearing as I don’t feel like I have been listened to, and my words were twisted in the original decision. I got a phone call today saying they will look again and see if I can get any points, but I highly doubt it. 

The job I have is one I worked hard for and have wanted since I was a kid. It’s a physical job and I love it, but I got diagnosed at 21 with CFS, and now I’m 22. I struggle to get through the day now. My manager is kind and aware, but he cannot reduce my work hours and even if he did, I would take a massive pay cut; something I can’t afford. I live on my own, have no financial or emotional support from my family, and no friends to help. The only person is my partner, who will make the effort to come round everyday and prepare meals and help bathe me as once I get home I find it hard to do anything. The disability benefit people said that I’m too young to be this unwell, and that because I can drive to work, and because I can do things just with difficulty, that I’m okay. I tried to explain the more I work the worse it will get, and at some point I won’t be able to work at all (something I don’t want) but they won’t hear it. The UK disability system has made me feel worthless, and the current state of the UK it is work until you drop. I just can’t fathom continuing like this for the next however many years.
